title: fix(spec,runtime,cli)!: the in-memory engine is no longer a boot store — every boot door refuses it and names SQLite instead
body:
Fixes #21492
Fixes #21572

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

## What this lands

One landing, as triage ruled (`5969348039`, (ii)): #21572's spec row and #21492's runtime and CLI halves. The in-memory (mingo) engine is retired as a **boot store**, at its declaration, on both hosts. It refuses every tenant-scoped read by design, so a boot on it signed the seeded admin in and then answered `503` to every data read. Every boot door now refuses it with one sentence that names the replacement: `os dev --fresh` for a throwaway database, or the URL `:memory:` for SQLite's own in-memory database.

- **spec** (`packages/spec/src/data/driver/config-registry.zod.ts`, the row from `d480ef0d70` plus its stale doc comments): `memory`, `mingo` and `in-memory` move from the selection face to `contractOnlyAliases`, beside `inmemory`. `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_ALIASES`, `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS`, the `--database-driver` allowlist and `--help` drop them by derivation. `resolveDriverId` is unchanged, so a stored `datasource.driver: memory` still parses. No artifact moves (`check:generated`: all 15 up to date).
- **runtime**:
  - `resolveProjectDatabaseUrl`: the `memory-driver` rung becomes a refusal that stands **ahead of every rung**. `ProjectDatabaseUrlSource` loses `'memory-driver'`.
  - `resolveStandaloneDatabase`: the URL detection recognises `memory://` and `mingo://`, and `refuseRetiredMemoryEngine` refuses them. It names the source: the typed URL, `OS_DATABASE_URL`, or the project's declared default datasource.
  - `unsupportedDriverMessage` gives a spelling of the engine the retirement sentence, not the typo list.
  - `StandaloneDatabaseDriverSchema` now enumerates the selection face. The dispatch loses its `memory` arm, and `ResolvedStandaloneDatabase.driver` can no longer name it.
  - The sentence lives in one place, `retiredMemoryEngineMessage`, with the predicate `namesRetiredMemoryEngine`. Both are exported for the CLI.
- **cli**:
  - `inferDriverTypeFromUrl` refuses `memory://` and `mingo://` with `UnsupportedDriverError` (`recognized: false`).
  - `resolveStorageDefinition` refuses the spellings with the same sentence. The `memory` definition arm is gone.
  - The `--database` help of `dev` and `start` offers `:memory:` instead of `memory://`.
  - The `storage-driver.ts` #3276 note and its module header are rewritten: the header now says which boots reach that file (legacy only). The parity pin's header, the `database-driver-flag.ts` doc and serve's comments are rewritten too.
- **docs**: `deployment/cli.mdx`, `deployment/environment-variables.mdx`, `data-modeling/drivers.mdx`, `plugins/index.mdx`.
- **QA** (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json`, revisions bumped with history):
  - `cli.dev-boot-contract`: the memory tier becomes a REFUSED variant, with a negative and the `:memory:` variant added.
  - `cli.migrate-duplicates-inventory`: the `no_sql_seam` negative cites the seam-double pin.
  - devx's rider `5967974683`: `cli.build-own-contract`'s six live strings name `this.exit(2)`. Its two dated history entries keep their wording, because they record what was true when written.
- **ledger**: `scripts/driver-memory-census.ledger.json`'s CLI row `why` no longer claims that a boot spelling routes to the driver.
- **one changeset** with the narrowing kit: `fix(...)!`, BREAKING, `minor` for the three packages, and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

The `driver-memory` package is unchanged. A declared non-default `driver: 'memory'` datasource and a directly constructed `InMemoryDriver` still build: per the ruling, neither is a boot spelling.

## A1: reach, measured on both trees

**Before**, on `origin/main` `901e7cf13a` with `examples/app-crm` (closure build exit 0, 60/60 tasks):

| invocation | result |
|---|---|
| `os dev --fresh --database-driver memory` | sign-in 200; `GET /api/v1/data/crm_lead` **503** `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; the banner shows `Database: file:/tmp/objectstack-dev-…/data/objectstack.db` beside `Driver: _InMemoryDriver → (in-memory)` (the banner finding) |
| `os migrate plan --database-url memory://qa` | **exit 0**, `datasource 'default': connected (driver=memory …)` |
| `os dev --fresh` (control) | sign-in 200; crm_lead **200**; `SqlDriver(better-sqlite3)` |

**After**, on this branch (`133871a251`; the refusal code has not changed since):

| door | result |
|---|---|
| `os dev --fresh --database-driver memory` | exit 2 at flag parse (oclif: `Expected --database-driver=memory to be one of: sqlite, sqlite-wasm, postgres, mysql, mongodb, turso`) |
| `os start --database-driver memory` | exit 2, same |
| `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=memory os dev --fresh` (and `mingo`) | exit 1 before any `Database:` row, naming `--fresh` and `:memory:` |
| `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=in-memory os start` | exit 1, same sentence |
| `os dev --fresh --database memory://x` | the parent prints `Database: memory://x`; the serve child refuses, exit 1 |
| `os migrate plan --database-url memory://qa` / `mingo://qa` | exit 1, `[StandaloneStack] The database URL "…" selects the in-memory (mingo) engine …` |
| `os migrate duplicates --database-url memory://qa` | exit 1, `{"error":"boot_failed", …}` with the sentence |
| `OS_MODE=legacy OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=memory os serve --dev` | exit 1 (legacy CLI host) |
| `OS_MODE=legacy OS_DATABASE_URL=mingo://x os serve --dev` | exit 1 (legacy CLI host, inference) |
| `OS_ARTIFACT_PATH=… OS_DATABASE_URL=memory:// os serve --dev` (artifact path, empty cwd) | exit 1 |
| `os dev --fresh` (control) | crm_lead **200**, `SqlDriver(better-sqlite3)` |
| `os dev --database :memory:` (the replacement) | crm_lead **200**, `Database: :memory:`, `SqlDriver(better-sqlite3) → :memory:` |

## A2: which doors reach which resolver (symbol walk)

- **Runtime host** (`resolveStandaloneDatabase`, which calls `resolveProjectDatabaseUrl`), reached by:
  - `os serve` over a config (`createStandaloneStack`) and over an artifact (`createDefaultHostConfig`, then `createStandaloneStack`); these are the serve children of `os dev` and `os start`;
  - every `bootSchemaStack` user: `os migrate` `apply`, `plan`, `meta`, `duplicates`, `account-issuer`, `audit-metadata-bodies`, `files-to-references`, `multi-value-columns`, `recorded-by`, `resume`, `summary-nulls` and `value-shapes`, plus `os meta resync`, `os secret orphans` / `rewrap` and `os storage orphans`;
  - `probeMigrationTarget`, the pre-boot probe of seven migrate subcommands;
  - every embedder.
- **The shared resolver alone** (`resolveProjectDatabaseUrl`), reached by the `os dev` and `os start` parents (`resolveDevDatabase`, `resolveStartDatabase`) and by `os db clean`.
- **CLI host** (`resolveDriverType` with `resolveStorageDefinition`), reached by `os serve`'s legacy path only: `OS_MODE=off|none|legacy`, `bootMode: 'off'`, or a host config (`shouldBootWithLibrary`).
- One refusal per host, at the resolver. No command carries a copy.

## A3: refusal shape and code

The refusals reuse each host's existing shape for an unrecognised driver or scheme: the runtime's plain `Error`, prefixed `[StandaloneStack]` inside the standalone stack, and the CLI's `UnsupportedDriverError`. No ledgered error code is involved, and the error-code ledger is not edited. The CLI flag door is oclif's own allowlist refusal, derived from the spec (see Acceptance notes).

## A4: parity pin

`driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts` is the pin, with no exemption:
- The accept rows still iterate the selection face, so the three spellings leave them by derivation.
- A new row asserts which spellings the table withdrew: contract face yes, selection face no, derived from `DRIVER_ID_ALIASES`.
- New refuse rows: both hosts refuse `memory` / `mingo` / `in-memory`, in dev and in prod, and both name `--fresh` and `:memory:`.
- New URL-door rows: both hosts refuse `memory://`, `memory://named`, `mingo://` and `MINGO://upper` with no driver named.
- A control: both hosts accept `:memory:` as `sqlite`.
- The `mingo://` cross-host divergence (the CLI accepted it, the runtime called it an unknown scheme) is closed: both hosts now recognise and refuse it.

## A5: the census ledger row

`scripts/driver-memory-census.ledger.json`, gated by `scripts/check-driver-memory-census.mjs`. The file is under `scripts/`: it is not `packages/spec` and not a governed surface. The CLI manifest row's `why` is rewritten, its axis is unchanged, and `check:driver-memory-census` is green.

## A6: reverse verification

Both legs were run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the committed tree (`b0b835ba75`), in WRAP mode, with a trap that restores from `HEAD` by absolute path.

- **Runtime leg.** Three sites were planted, each behind an `OS_ABLATION_RUNTIME_*` env marker: the rung refusal, `refuseRetiredMemoryEngine`, and the `unsupportedDriverMessage` branch. Each anchor went 1 to 0, and each blob changed.
  - Runtime rebuilt (exit 0); `ablation-dist-preflight` found all three markers in `dist/` (exit 0 each).
  - Runtime pins: **14 red** of 124, in 4 files.
  - CLI: `dev-default-db` 2 red; the parity pin 7 red, each failing on its **runtime-half** lines (`:231`, `:254`).
  - `storage-driver.test.ts` (the CLI host): **green**.
  - Restore: blob equals `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty. Runtime rebuilt; `preflight --absent` exit 0 for all three markers.
- **CLI leg.** Two sites were planted in `storage-driver.ts`, the inference refusal and the spelling refusal; the anchors went 1 to 0. The tests import that file from source, so no build was involved.
  - `storage-driver.test.ts`: **9 red**. The parity pin: 7 red, each failing on its **CLI-half** lines (`:225`, `:248`).
  - The other host stays **green**: runtime pins 124/124, and `dev-default-db` (runtime-backed).
  - Restore: blob equals `HEAD`, 0 markers left, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Tests and gates (at `b0b835ba75`)

- **Full suites:**
  - `@objectstack/runtime` (all projects): 319 files, 5210 passed and 19 skipped.
  - `@objectstack/cli` `--project unit`: 254 files, 3742 passed.
  - `@objectstack/spec`: 657 files, 18834 passed and 1 todo.
- **CLI integration**, the 19 integration-tier files that boot `os migrate` / `bootSchemaStack` or spawn `serve` with a store flag or URL: 19 files, 210 passed and 1 skipped. `duplicates.null-seam.test.ts` now boots nothing, so the tier predicate files it under `unit`.
- **Typecheck:** runtime, cli and spec typecheck all exit 0, test-typecheck debt held.
- **Lint:** the full `pnpm lint` exits 0.
- **Spec artifacts:** `@objectstack/spec check:generated` exits 0.
- **Derived gates:** `dispatch-gates --commands` (no paths) derived 121 for the 31 changed paths, and all 121 exit 0. `--ran` reports 121 run and 0 NOT-MEASURED. Three of them (`check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n-coverage`) first exited 3 for a missing build. They were re-run after a full `turbo run build --filter=!@objectstack/docs` (exit 0) and exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- **The flag door names no replacement.** `--database-driver memory` is refused by oclif's derived allowlist, in oclif's wording. It lists the legal kinds, `sqlite` among them, but does not name `--fresh` or `:memory:`. Making it do so would mean dropping the derived `options:` or special-casing a value at the consumer. Both are forbidden by `database-driver-flag.ts` and by the ruling. Every other door names the replacement.
- **The URL door refuses after the parent's banner.** `os dev --database memory://x` prints the parent's `Database: memory://x` row, and the serve child then refuses, naming `OS_DATABASE_URL` (the channel it received the URL on). This is the same shape every unsupported scheme already has. The driver spelling is refused before the banner. The banner finding (a `file:` row beside an in-memory child) cannot occur any more.
- **The CLI's `@objectstack/driver-memory` dependency** now serves no CLI-owned path. The ledger row says so. It is kept, because removing a published dependency is a packaging decision the ruling did not take. Carrier: none.
- `duplicates.ts`'s header still quotes the original `memory://qa` measurement. That is a dated record of the defect, not an instruction.
